children: has started switching off its “Find Friends” feature by default for children in the UK, following pressure from the British media regulator Ofcom to strengthen safeguards against online grooming, Reuters reported on Friday.

The move, announced by Ofcom on Friday, is intended to limit opportunities for strangers to connect with children through the platform. The regulator said it would closely monitor the implementation of the measure this month.
had pledged to introduce the change in May and has subsequently told Ofcom that it expects effective age-verification measures for users under 18 to be operational by year-end.
Ofcom cited the platform’s popularity among younger users, noting that 32% of British children aged 8 to 12 used Snapchat
despite its minimum age requirement of 13.
The concerns are underscored by a 2025 analysis of police data by the NSPCC, which found that Snapchat
accounted for 40% of recorded offenses involving sexual communication with children where a platform was identified.
Ofcom warned other technology companies that failure to address grooming risks could result in penalties of up to 10% of qualifying global revenue.

title: Snapchat disables friend-finder feature for UK children amid safety concerns
